corrected_statement: Open question, still unmeasured. A model edit needs a host mj_compile ('1 call per new field instance'), put_model and a new graph capture; per-world parameter values are batched model fields and need no recompilation. auditor: AUD01 independent auditor (fresh agent, no authorship of the claims)
corrected_statement: The rule controls false confirmation (a true 5x passes in about 0% of simulated campaigns) but is under-powered as specified. Each brief needs a point estimate of at least 10, so a true ratio of exactly 10 passes a brief about half the time at any seed count, and the conjunction of four of six briefs including both held-out ones then passes in at most 18% of campaigns, and in 0 to 11% with five seeds. With five seeds and a log standard deviation of 0.5 the rule reaches 80% power only near a true 20x. Re-specify before use: test a pooled ratio whose lower bound exceeds 5, say whether the bound is one- or two-sided, define what happens when a median is censored, and use at least ten seeds per arm.

auditor: AUD01 independent auditor (fresh agent, no authorship of the claims)
corrected_statement: With equal agent latency of 60 to 120 s per turn and about 300 s of incumbent training, a loop that evaluates one design per turn is capped at 3.5 to 6x per turn even if FrankenRobotics' compute time falls to zero. Reaching tenfold wall-clock on quadruped-class briefs therefore needs at least one more multiplicative factor. Designs decided per agent turn is one; fewer turns to reach a qualified design (better diagnostics, static pruning) and lower agent latency per turn (smaller telemetry to read) are others, and time to qualified design is their product. 'The only route' is not established. The batching route is also open to the incumbent arm, since MuJoCo Warp documents batched model fields, so it differentiates only together with a controller that needs no per-design training.
